descriptionChirho: To cover or overlay a surface (typically wood) with a layer of metal such as gold, bronze, or silver, used extensively of tabernacle and temple construction (Piel active).
The passive state of being overlaid or plated with metal, describing an object that has been covered with gold or another precious material (Pual participle).

To spread out or set something in place, a distinct Qal usage diverging from the Piel overlaying sense, with multilingual evidence suggesting either spreading a covering or possibly a homophonous root related to watching or observing.
